ABOUT THE CENTER

Mission and Vision

As the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area accelerates the development of an international science and technology innovation center, life sciences face a historic opportunity for deeper integration of industry, universities and research.

Under the leadership of Dean Mingjie Zhang, the School of Life Sciences at Southern University of Science and Technology has established strengths in frontier disciplines including structural biology, neuroscience and synthetic biology.

In response to the national innovation-driven development strategy and Shenzhen’s “20+8” industrial cluster plan for biomedicine and health, the center builds a hub integrating technology translation, academic exchange and interdisciplinary talent development. It breaks down traditional barriers between academia and industry and creates an efficient, coordinated innovation ecosystem connecting industry, universities, research and application, significantly strengthening the school’s capacity to generate scientific and technological innovation, its industrial influence and its development of interdisciplinary talent in life, health, biomedicine and other frontier fields.

PEOPLE & LEADERSHIP

Core Members

Director

Mingjie Zhang

Chair Professor; Dean of the School of Life Sciences; Member of the Chinese Academy of Sciences; Founding Member of the Hong Kong Academy of Sciences.

Biography

He received the Outstanding Scholar Award from the Croucher Foundation in Hong Kong in 2003 and the Second Prize of the State Natural Science Award in 2006. In 2011, he received the Ho Leung Ho Lee Foundation Prize for Science and Technology and was elected to the Chinese Academy of Sciences. He became a Founding Member of the Hong Kong Academy of Sciences in 2015 and received the Tan Jiazhen Life Science Achievement Award in 2021.

Deputy Director

Rowan Wang

Professor · Joint appointment in the Business School and School of Life Sciences

Biography

He received the Third Prize of the Zhejiang Provincial Science and Technology Progress Award. His decision-making advisory report was accepted by the General Office of the State Council, and his policy research report received written comments from the Secretary of the CPC Zhejiang Provincial Committee.

He has been selected as a young distinguished expert under the national overseas high-level talent recruitment program, a leading young talent under Guangdong’s Pearl River Talent Program, and a distinguished professor under Shenzhen’s Pengcheng Peacock Program, among other honors.

WHAT WE DO

Closing the loop between industry, universities and research

Select a segment to explore our work

01 / 04

Five research directions

Translational Research

The five focus areas are structural biology, synthetic biology, cell therapy, neuroscience and biomedical engineering. A seed fund supports early-stage research with clear translational potential.

Research, education and industry working together

02 / 04

Identifying and matching needs

Industry–University Partnerships

Identifying and matching needs: conduct in-depth company research to pinpoint technical challenges, review the school’s research outputs and actively introduce them to companies. Joint research platforms: organize university–industry laboratories, technology assessment and incubation for industry-sponsored projects.

Research, education and industry working together

03 / 04

Courses and projects

Interdisciplinary Talent Development Base

Courses and projects: offer innovation and entrepreneurship courses and face-to-face exchanges with successful entrepreneurs. Internships and practice: establish a network of company internship bases and involve students deeply in the full R&D process of the center’s industry-sponsored projects. Entrepreneurship guidance, seed funding and incubation space support faculty and students in launching ventures based on the center’s research outputs.

Research, education and industry working together

04 / 04

“Life Sciences + X” joint research

Interdisciplinary Research Across Multiple Fields

Break down disciplinary barriers within the school and form “Life Sciences + X” joint research teams. Support exploratory interdisciplinary research through seed projects and joint projects, enabling research collaboration across multiple fields.

Research, education and industry working together

PROJECT PARTNERSHIPS

Project Partnerships

Strategic Funding

Strategic funding partnerships have been secured for the school

Health services throughout childhood

Chongqing Xiaomixiong Children’s Hospital Co., Ltd.

Specializing in children’s health, the company focuses on full-lifecycle health services for children aged 0–18 and is a distinctive pediatric healthcare provider in Southwest China.

In-depth medical–engineering collaboration

Shenzhen Rongyi Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.

The company specializes in R&D, production and sales in low-altitude security. It will undertake in-depth medical–engineering collaboration with the health innovation center, drawing on drone-based low-altitude monitoring and other technical strengths to enable a range of health applications.

Interdisciplinary Collaborative Projects

01 / Emergency response

Coordinated air–ground emergency response network

Ruiying Emergency Eye

Build a coordinated air–ground emergency response network connecting people, aircraft and vehicles; make the most of the critical first four minutes after cardiac arrest; close gaps in prehospital emergency care in complex settings; strengthen public emergency services; and use technology to protect lives.

Project description ＋

Close gaps in prehospital emergency care in complex settings, strengthen public emergency services and use technology to protect lives.

02 / Synthetic biology

LLPS Scaffold Protein Design and Optimization

Environmentally Robust
Efficient LLPS Scaffold Protein
Design and Optimization

Establish design principles for condensates that are insensitive to cell type, expression fluctuations and environmental perturbations, serving artificial membraneless organelles, reaction pathway compartmentalization, signaling regulation, cell factories and therapeutic cell engineering.

Project description ＋

Serve artificial membraneless organelles, reaction pathway compartmentalization, signaling regulation, cell factories and therapeutic cell engineering.

03 / Drug discovery

AI-Driven RNA Drug Discovery

AI-Driven
RNA Drug Discovery

Developed by the research teams of Professors Wei Chen and Zefeng Wang at SUSTech School of Life Sciences, this project creates an AI-driven platform for innovative RNA drug discovery. It uses large AI models to perform RNA sequence optimization, molecular screening and delivery system design, connecting the R&D pipeline from target discovery and molecular design through LNP delivery optimization to preclinical validation.

Project description ＋
